chapter_title: Chương 62: 0062【Ngồi chung bàn với các nhà văn】

segments.title: Chương 62: 0062【Ngồi chung bàn với các nhà văn】
segments.content:
After the awards were presented, there were various speeches.

As the chairman of the finals judging committee, Wang Meng was the first to take the stage. "The New Concept Composition Competition has, in the blink of an eye, been running for six years since its inception. The young people who won awards in the first and second competitions have already grown into adults..."

"During these six years, we have discovered many outstanding young people. Some have already become writers, others..."

"I am very honored to once again serve as the chairman of the judging committee this year. I've read many fine essays. The sharp thinking and fresh writing style of these young people have been a great source of inspiration, even for an old man like myself..."

"What's most remarkable is that this year produced yet another masterful work... It is very difficult to write a good essay for a three-hour impromptu topic. Not only is student Chen Guiliang's essay lofty in its conception and unique in its perspective, but it is written entirely in classical prose and poetry. He not only managed to write it, but it is also filled with brilliant lines that are truly astonishing..."

"The renowned professors and writers on our judging committee all heaped praise upon this essay. However, there is still some debate regarding its interpretation. I think we could very well hold another seminar, invite the author to join us for a chat, and appreciate this masterpiece more directly..."

"This year's competition has been a great success. I hope we can build on this next year, with more outstanding young people signing up to compete, and that we will see even more refreshing and excellent essays emerge..."

Next, the admissions director from Peking University came on stage to give a speech.

Why not Tsinghua?

Because the one from Peking University held a higher position; his title was Dean of the Faculty, while Tsinghua had only sent a department head.

The New Concept Composition Competition organizing committee was the same. Peking University's Vice President appeared in person, while Tsinghua sent its Dean of Academic Affairs.

After that, Mengya's editor-in-chief, Zhao Changtian, gave a speech.

In the previous competitions, the speeches ended here. There was never anything for the award-winning contestants.

But then they heard Li Qigang, the competition's general director, say, "Now, let's invite student Chen Guiliang to give a speech on behalf of this year's award-winning contestants!"

The first-prize winners from Groups A, B, and C were all sitting in the audience at this moment.

Mi Lan said in surprise, "There's a speech segment for contestants?"

"I don't think there was before," Luo Jin shook her head. "I heard from a senior at my school that he left right after the leaders' speeches. He even had lunch on the train."

Chen Guiliang was already prepared, because Hu Weishi had asked him to write a speech just this morning.

"Respected leaders, teachers, seniors, and fellow students: It is with great excitement and, at the same time, trepidation that I have the honor of giving this speech on behalf of the contestants. All the participants are truly outstanding, and I am just a very ordinary one among them..."

Chen Guiliang had already stolen enough of the limelight; there was no need to say anything shocking in his speech.

With a very humble attitude, he delivered a speech full of empty, formal pleasantries. Things like thanking the competition organizers for the opportunity, thanking the judges for their recognition, thanking the admissions officers for their favor, thanking his parents and school teachers... and so on and so forth.

Finally, he wished the New Concept Composition Competition continued success.

*Clap clap clap clap...*

Chen Guiliang stepped down from the stage amidst a round of applause.

Aside from a few contestants who found his speech disingenuous, long-winded, and tedious, the adults present were all very satisfied with his performance.

How high could one's expectations be for a high school student?

Being poised and not getting stage fright was good enough.

What's more, Chen Guiliang appeared calm and composed, his delivery was well-paced and articulate, and he was modest and prudent without being ostentatious.

And with that, the morning's events came to a close.

The contestants who won second prize or lower could go home directly. They could stay if they wanted, but they'd have to cover their own room and board.

First-prize winners could stay or leave. Their lunch was covered by the competition organizers, and they could also sit in on the seminar in the afternoon.

As for the media reporters, of course, their food and drink were also free, and by the way... they would go collect their travel expenses.

Did you think the reporters came all this way for free?

They had to be paid!

The more remote the location, the lower the status of the organization, the more a reporter had to be paid in travel expenses to get the media to show up.

For example, if Chen Guiliang returned to his school and No. 2 High wanted to invite the media for publicity, they would have to give the reporters sufficient travel expenses. At current rates, a single reporter would cost at least several thousand yuan, and some major newspapers might even command tens of thousands.

Of course, the media invited by New Concept this time were all local, as well as reporters stationed in Shanghai by out-of-town media outlets. Since the journey was short and didn't take up much time, and Mengya was a major organization, one or two thousand yuan per reporter was enough.

Chen Guiliang headed straight for the tables where the first-prize winners were seated, but was called to a halt halfway by Hu Weishi. "Chen Guiliang, the writers are calling you over!"

"Just a moment."

After saying that, Chen Guiliang ran downstairs to the hotel room to grab two books.

Hu Weishi waited for him in the corridor and asked when he came out, "What are you doing?"

Chen Guiliang held up the books and smiled. "Getting autographs for my cousin."

In fact, Tao Xue had only asked for autographs from Yu Hua and Su Tong, but Chen Guiliang had taken it upon himself to buy one of Wang Meng's representative works as well.

Hu Weishi led him upstairs, reminding him, "When you're eating with the famous authors and professors, be careful what you say. Don't offend someone by accident."

"Understood," Chen Guiliang agreed.

He wasn't foolish enough to directly challenge Fang Fang.

What would come of arguing with her?

"Great talent, come on over!" Tie Ning waved enthusiastically.

A seat had been saved for Chen Guiliang between Wang Meng and Tie Ning.

Chen Guiliang quickened his pace and shook Tie Ning's hand, saying, "Teacher Tie, hello."

Tie Ning smiled. "So you recognize me."

"I've read your works and seen your photo in books," Chen Guiliang said. "I didn't expect you to be even more beautiful in person than in your photos."

Tie Ning was extremely pleased by this and immediately burst into laughter.

Chen Guiliang had indeed read this female writer's books; her early works were quite good.

Tie Ning helped with the introductions. "I'm sure I don't need to introduce this one, do I?"

Chen Guiliang extended both hands. "Teacher Wang, hello."

"Hello," Wang Meng said with emotion. "I've been wanting to talk to you ever since I read your essay yesterday. This young man has limitless potential."

Chen Guiliang said, "My crude work is merely a source of amusement for esteemed experts."

Wang Meng said, "Young people shouldn't be too modest. Bring out that 'who else but me' spirit from your essay."

Yu Hua chimed in from the side, "I've already seen that kind of spirit. The day before yesterday, I was returning to my hotel when I heard someone shout, 'Yu Hua, stop right there!' It gave me a scare. I thought someone had read 'To Live' and was angry enough to come beat me up. Turns out, they were just looking for an autograph."

"Hahaha!"

The crowd roared with laughter.

The members of the judging committee occupied two tables, one for writers and one for professors.

The writers were Wang Meng, Tie Ning, Yu Hua, Su Tong, Ma Yuan, Cheng Cun, Ye Xin, Fang Fang, Ye Zhaoyan, and Sun Ganlu.

The professors were from ten different universities.

Tie Ning pulled Chen Guiliang along, introducing him one by one. Fang Fang seemed a bit displeased.

This had nothing to do with Chen Guiliang; it was purely a subtle rivalry between the two female writers.

Among all the writers present, they were the only two women. Tie Ning had directly pulled Chen Guiliang over, acting like the female host, which made Fang Fang feel she had lost face.

What are you so smug about?

After the introductions were complete, Chen Guiliang finally sat down.

Yu Hua asked, "Do you drink?"

"I can have a little," Chen Guiliang said.

"Then pour him one!"

Ma Yuan pushed the liquor bottle over.

The writers all began to jeer, saying that Chen Guiliang was late and had to be penalized with a drink first.

Chen Guiliang had no choice but to drink it.

"Damn, that essay of yours is fucking incredible. How did you write it?" Yu Hua took out a cigarette and stuck it in his mouth, then casually tossed cigarettes to the other male writers.

Chen Guiliang said, "I originally wrote it in vernacular, but the emotional impact wasn't quite there, so I just decided to rewrite it using classical prose and poetry."

Yu Hua chuckled. "When I read your preliminary round essay, I thought you had someone ghostwrite it."

"It was just an unconventional approach. Classical Chinese is more eye-catching," Chen Guiliang said.

Cheng Cun took a bite of food and said while chewing, "Come write for Under the Banyan Tree when you have time. Young people need to be good at using the internet."

Chen Guiliang asked, "Does Teacher Cheng still hold a position at Under the Banyan Tree?"

"I'm the Artistic Director for Under the Banyan Tree. The website pays me a salary, so I have to help recruit people," Cheng Cun said.

Chen Guiliang said, "Since Teacher Cheng has extended the invitation, I'll submit something to Under the Banyan Tree when I get the chance."

Ma Yuan puffed out a cloud of smoke and said, "Tongji doesn't have a partnership with New Concept. But if you want to come to Tongji, I can help you secure a spot. I can be your advisor for your master's and doctorate degrees then."

"Hey, Old Ma, are you trying to poach him already?" Su Tong said. "Chen Guiliang, you should come to our Beijing Normal University instead. The Chinese department at BNU is much better than Tongji's."

Ma Yuan cursed with a laugh, "Fuck, I'm a professor at Tongji, so it's only natural for me to recruit for the university. You're not a BNU professor, what are you getting involved for?"

"I'm a BNU alumnus," Su Tong said.

Wang Meng spoke up, "Alright now, the admissions people are at that table. Let's not talk about this."

These writers managed to maintain a modicum of decorum in public, but at the dinner table, most of them dropped the act.

After three or five drinks, they were talking about all sorts of things, and even the female writers started cursing.

At first, the conversation revolved around Chen Guiliang, but gradually they broke off into their own separate chats.

In March, two of them were going to France for the Paris Book Fair. They were discussing where to meet up and fly over together. Others asked them to act as purchasing agents and bring back some luxury goods for their wives.

As they chatted, the topic drifted to French cinema, art, and literature.

Some of the writers praised France to the high heavens, as if even a female French mosquito was sexy and romantic.

Chen Guiliang ate his food silently, feeling as if he were listening to his political science teacher brag. It was essentially the same thing, a kind of lack of confidence in one's own country's economy and culture.

At this stage, it was completely understandable.

Because most people had come from that mindset, and perceptions needed to change slowly with the times.

Those who couldn't change would inevitably be left behind by the times!

Seeing that they had had enough to drink, Chen Guiliang finally took out the two books and went to ask Wang Meng and Su Tong for their autographs.

He made sure to emphasize that they were for his cousin, so as not to make the other writers lose face.

"Let's go, let's go, time for the seminar," Yu Hua, who had had a bit too much to drink, slung an arm around Chen Guiliang's shoulders, holding his down jacket in the other hand.

A whiff of smoke and alcohol hit him, and Chen Guiliang really wanted to push him away.

The other first-prize winners, seeing how close Chen Guiliang and Yu Hua were, were all incredibly envious.

The seminar was to be held in a large hall, but it wouldn't start for a little while yet.

Reporters from thirty or forty media outlets took the opportunity to interview the famous writers and professors. Very few, however, interviewed Chen Guiliang.

Because they could also ask Chen Guiliang questions during the seminar.

"Hello, Chen Guiliang." A female reporter in her thirties walked over.

"Hello."

"I'm Zhang Xinping, a reporter from the Shanghai Youth Daily. May I interview you for a moment?"

"It would be my honor."
